label: First Debate On Radio Only
detail: The first joint broadcast of the two nominees in September 1960 is carried on radio alone, so voters hear the candidates but do not see them.
assumption: Voters who followed the first debate judge the nominees by their words and voices alone, so appearance and manner on screen no longer shape impressions. Television audiences shrink and the debate's effect on undecided voters is muted.
facts_text: The first of the joint appearances by the two major presidential nominees was broadcast on radio only, with no television coverage.
Listeners across the country heard the nominees answer questions on domestic policy, but no pictures of the appearance were shown.
research_questions: How did radio listeners and television viewers of the September 1960 debate differ in judging who performed better?
How many voters said the debates influenced their choice, and which voters were they?
How did the nominees' appearance and manner on television affect impressions among undecided voters?
source_text: the first debate is on radio only.
